sentences.zh: 慕容超

translations.literal: Murong Chao
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao

sentences.zh: 慕容超字祖明，德兄北海王納之子。

translations.literal: Murong Chao’s courtesy name was Zuming; he was the son of Na, Prince of Beihai, elder brother of Murong De.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao, style Zuming, was the son of Murong Na, Prince of Beihai—Murong De’s elder brother.

sentences.zh: 苻堅破鄴，以納為廣武太守，數歲去官，家於張掖。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian took Ye, he appointed Na as governor of Guangwu; after several years Na left office and made his home in Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian seized Ye, Murong Na served as governor of Guangwu, then retired to Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 德之南征，留金刀而去。

translations.literal: When De campaigned south, he left a golden knife and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De marched south, leaving a golden knife as a token.

sentences.zh: 及垂起兵山東，苻昌收納及德諸子，皆誅之。

translations.literal: When Chui raised troops in Shandong, Fu Chang seized Na and De’s sons and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Chui rose in Shandong, Fu Chang arrested Murong Na and Murong De’s sons and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 納母公孫氏以耄獲免，納妻段氏方娠，未決，囚之於郡獄。

translations.literal: Na’s mother Lady Gongsun was spared because of extreme age; Na’s wife Lady Duan was pregnant and her case undecided, so she was imprisoned in the commandery jail.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gongsun was spared as a crone; Lady Duan, still pregnant, languished in the county prison.

sentences.zh: 獄掾呼延平，德之故吏也，嘗有死罪，德免之。

translations.literal: The jail clerk Huyan Ping had been an old subordinate of De’s; he once faced a capital crime, which De pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The warden Huyan Ping, once spared from death by Murong De, owed him a life.

sentences.zh: 至是，將公孫及段氏逃於羌中，而生超焉。

translations.literal: At this point he led Gongsun and Lady Duan to flee among the Qiang, and there Chao was born.
translations.idiomatic: He smuggled the women into Qiang territory, where Murong Chao was born.

sentences.zh: 年十歲而公孫氏卒，臨終授超以金刀，曰：「若天下太平，汝得東歸，可以此刀還汝叔也。

translations.literal: At age ten Gongsun died; on her deathbed she handed Chao the golden knife, saying: “If the realm is at peace and you can return east, you may give this knife back to your uncle.”
translations.idiomatic: At ten he lost Lady Gongsun, who gave him the golden knife: if peace returned and he could go east, he was to restore it to his uncle.

sentences.zh: 」平又將超母子奔于呂光。

translations.literal: ” Ping then led Chao and his mother to flee to Lü Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Huyan Ping then fled with mother and son to Lü Guang.

sentences.zh: 及呂隆降于姚興，超又隨涼州人徙于長安。

translations.literal: When Lü Long surrendered to Yao Xing, Chao again followed Liangzhou people to be relocated to Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Long submitted to Yao Xing, Murong Chao was marched to Chang’an with the Liangzhou exiles.

sentences.zh: 超母謂超曰：「吾母子全濟，呼延氏之力。

translations.literal: Chao’s mother said to Chao: “Our mother and son were wholly saved through the power of the Huyan clan.”
translations.idiomatic: His mother reminded him the Huyan clan had saved their lives.

sentences.zh: 平今雖死，吾欲為汝納其女以答厚惠。

translations.literal: Though Ping is dead now, I wish to take his daughter for you in marriage to repay his great kindness.”
translations.idiomatic: Though Huyan Ping was dead, she would marry his daughter to him in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 」於是娶之。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he married her.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao wed her.

sentences.zh: 超自以諸父在東，恐為姚氏所錄，乃陽狂行乞。

translations.literal: Chao, because his uncles were in the east, feared the Yao clan would register and detain him, and therefore feigned madness and begged in the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Yao Xing would cage him while his kinsmen ruled the east, he played the mad beggar.

sentences.zh: 秦人賤之，惟姚紹見而異焉，勸興拘以爵位。

translations.literal: The people of Qin despised him; only Yao Shao saw him and thought him unusual, urging Xing to bind him with office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Qin folk scorned him, but Yao Shao saw something in him and urged an appointment.

sentences.zh: 召見與語，超深自晦匿，興大鄙之，謂紹曰：「諺雲'妍皮不裹癡骨'，妄語耳。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience and conversation, Chao deeply hid his light; Xing greatly despised him and said to Shao: “The proverb says ‘fair skin does not wrap foolish bones’—empty talk.”
translations.idiomatic: At audience Murong Chao played the dullard; Yao Xing sneered that “pretty skin doesn’t hide a stupid skull.”

sentences.zh: 」由是得去來無禁。

translations.literal: ” On that account he was allowed to come and go without restriction.
translations.idiomatic: He was left free to roam.

sentences.zh: 德遣使迎之，超不告母妻乃歸。

translations.literal: De sent envoys to welcome him; Chao returned without telling his mother or wife.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong De summoned him, he slipped away without a word to mother or wife.

sentences.zh: 及至廣固，呈以金刀，具宣祖母臨終之言，德撫之號慟。

translations.literal: When he reached Guanggu, he presented the golden knife and fully relayed his grandmother’s dying words; De embraced him and wailed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: At Guanggu he produced the golden knife and his grandmother’s charge; Murong De wept and held him close.

sentences.zh: 超身長八尺，腰帶九圍，精彩秀髮，容止可觀。

translations.literal: Chao’s body was eight chi tall, his girdle nine spans round, his spirit bright and hair splendid, his bearing presentable.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi, with a nine-span waist, brilliant eyes, luxuriant hair, and princely bearing.

sentences.zh: 德甚加禮遇，始名之曰超，封北海王，拜侍中、驃騎大將軍、司隸校尉，開府，置佐吏。

translations.literal: De treated him with great courtesy, for the first time naming him Chao, enfeoffing him Prince of Beihai, appointing him palace attendant, chief general of the vanguard, colonel director of the retainers, opening an office and installing aides.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De named him Chao, made him Prince of Beihai, palace attendant, vanguard general, metropolitan commandant, with full staff.

sentences.zh: 德無子，欲以超為嗣，故為超起第于萬春門內，朝夕觀之。

translations.literal: De had no sons and wished to make Chao his heir, therefore built a mansion for Chao inside the Wanchun Gate, observing him morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Heirless, Murong De built Murong Chao a mansion inside Wanchun Gate and watched him constantly.

sentences.zh: 超亦深達德旨，入則盡歡承奉，出則傾身下士，於是內外稱美焉。

translations.literal: Chao also deeply grasped De’s intent: within he gave full joyful service; without he humbled himself to men of talent—thereupon inside and outside praised his beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao played the dutiful nephew at home and the humble patron of talent abroad, winning praise.

sentences.zh: 頃之，立為太子。

translations.literal: Before long he was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was named heir.

sentences.zh: 及德死，以僭嗣偽位，大赦境內，改元曰太上。

translations.literal: When De died, he succeeded to the usurped throne, granted great amnesty within the realm, and changed the era name to Taishang.
translations.idiomatic: On Murong De’s death he took the throne, amnestied the realm, and adopted the reign title Taishang.

sentences.zh: 尊德妻段氏為皇太后。

translations.literal: He honored De’s wife Lady Duan as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Duan, Murong De’s widow, became empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 以慕容鐘都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，慕容法為征南、都督徐、兗、揚、南兗四州諸軍事，慕容鎮加開府儀同三司、尚書令，封孚為太尉，鞠仲為司空，潘聰為左光祿大夫，封嵩為尚書左僕射，自余封拜各有差。

translations.literal: He appointed Murong Zhong area commander of all military affairs at court and recorder of the Secretariat, Murong Fa as conqueror of the south and area commander of Xu, Yan, Yang, and southern Yan, Murong Zhen added opening office with ceremonial parity to the Three Dukes and minister secretary, Feng Fu as grand commandant, Ju Zhong minister of works, Pan Cong left counselor guanglu, Feng Song left vice director of the Secretariat; the rest received graded investitures and appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He stacked the government with Murong Zhong, Murong Fa, Murong Zhen, Feng Fu, Ju Zhong, Pan Cong, Feng Song, and others in high posts.

sentences.zh: 後又以鐘為青州牧，段宏為徐州剌史，公孫五樓為武衛將軍、領屯騎校尉，內參政事。

translations.literal: Later he also made Zhong shepherd of Qingzhou, Duan Hong inspector of Xu, Gongsun Wulou guard general of the martial guard and concurrent colonel of the encampment cavalry, participating in government within.
translations.idiomatic: Later Murong Zhong held Qingzhou, Duan Hong Xu, and Gongsun Wulou mixed martial guard and palace cavalry roles at court.

sentences.zh: 封孚言於超曰：「臣聞五大不在邊，五細不在庭。

translations.literal: Feng Fu spoke to Chao: “Your servant has heard that the five great should not be on the frontier and the five slight should not be in the court.”
translations.idiomatic: Feng Fu cited the rule that great ministers stay at court, petty ones on the marches.

sentences.zh: 鐘，國之宗臣，社稷所賴；

translations.literal: Zhong is a pillar of the state on which the altars rely;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Zhong was a pillar of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 宏，外戚懿望，親賢具瞻。

translations.literal: Hong is a paragon of the outer kin, kin and worthy both looked up to.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Hong, imperial in-law and proven talent, commanded respect.

sentences.zh: 正應參翼百揆，不宜遠鎮方外。

translations.literal: They ought rightly to assist the hundred directors, not be garrisoned far outside.
translations.idiomatic: Both belonged in the capital, not on distant frontiers.

sentences.zh: 今鍾等出籓，五樓內輔，臣竊未安。

translations.literal: Now that Zhong and the others go out to screens while Wulou assists within, your servant privately is not at ease.”
translations.idiomatic: Sending Zhong abroad while Gongsun Wulou ruled within unsettled him.

sentences.zh: 」超新即位，害鐘等權逼，以問五樓。

translations.literal: Chao had newly ascended the throne and feared Zhong and the others’ power pressed on him; he consulted Wulou.
translations.idiomatic: The new king, jealous of Murong Zhong’s clout, asked Gongsun Wulou.

sentences.zh: 五樓欲專斷朝政，不欲鐘等在內，屢有間言，孚說竟不行。

translations.literal: Wulou wished to monopolize court government and did not want Zhong and the others within; repeatedly he spoke divisively; Fu’s advice in the end was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Wulou wanted sole power and poisoned Murong Chao against them; Feng Fu’s counsel died unheard.

sentences.zh: 鐘、宏俱有不平之色，相謂曰：「黃犬之皮恐當終補狐裘也。

translations.literal: Zhong and Hong both showed discontent; they said to each other: “The yellow dog’s hide will surely end up patching the fox fur.”
translations.idiomatic: Murong Zhong and Duan Hong muttered that cheap leather would patch noble fur—meaning they were being used.

sentences.zh: 」五樓聞之，嫌隙漸遘。

translations.literal: ” When Wulou heard it, suspicion and rift gradually deepened.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Wulou heard and nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 初，超自長安行至梁父，慕容法時為兗州，鎮南長史悅壽還謂法曰：「向見北海王子，天資弘雅，神爽高邁，始知天族多奇，玉林皆寶。

translations.literal: At first, when Chao traveled from Chang’an to Liangfu, Murong Fa then held Yan Province; the southern garrison chief clerk Yue Shou returned and said to Fa: “Just now I saw the prince of Beihai—his heaven-bestowed breadth is refined, his spirit lofty; only then did I know the celestial clan has many marvels, every tree of the jade grove a treasure.”
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Chao passed Liangfu, Yue Shou rhapsodized to Murong Fa about the princely refugee’s noble air.

sentences.zh: 」法曰：「昔成方遂詐稱衛太子，人莫辯之，此復天族乎？

translations.literal: ” Fa said: “Anciently Cheng Fangsui falsely claimed to be Crown Prince Wei—no one could tell; is this again the celestial clan?”
translations.idiomatic: Murong Fa sneered that impostors like Cheng Fangsui had fooled the world before.

sentences.zh: 」超聞而恚恨，形於言色。

translations.literal: When Chao heard it he harbored rage and resentment, shown in word and face.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao heard and never forgave him.

sentences.zh: 法亦怒，處之外館，由是結憾。

translations.literal: Fa also grew angry, lodged him in an outer hostel, and on that account they formed a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Fa housed him like a stranger; the feud hardened.

sentences.zh: 及德死，法又不奔喪，超遣使讓焉。

translations.literal: When De died, Fa again did not go to mourning; Chao sent envoys to reproach him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Fa skipped the funeral; Murong Chao sent a rebuke.

sentences.zh: 法常懼禍至，因此遂與慕容鐘、段宏等謀反。

translations.literal: Fa always feared disaster would come; on this account he then plotted rebellion with Murong Zhong, Duan Hong, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing payback, Murong Fa conspired with Murong Zhong and Duan Hong.

sentences.zh: 超知而征之，鐘稱疾不赴，於是收其党侍中慕容統、右衛慕容根、散騎常侍段封誅之，車裂僕射封嵩於東門之外。

translations.literal: Chao learned of it and summoned them; Zhong claimed illness and did not go; thereupon he seized their faction—palace attendant Murong Tong, right guard Murong Gen, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary Duan Feng—and executed them, and tore Vice Director Feng Song apart with carts outside the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao struck first: Murong Zhong feigned illness; the king executed Murong Tong, Murong Gen, Duan Feng, and had Feng Song torn by chariots.

sentences.zh: 西中郎將封融奔于魏。

translations.literal: West Palace General Feng Rong fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: General Feng Rong defected to Wei.

sentences.zh: 超尋遣慕容鎮等攻青州，慕容昱等攻徐州，慕容凝、韓范攻梁父。

translations.literal: Chao soon sent Murong Zhen and others to attack Qingzhou, Murong Yu and others to attack Xu, Murong Ning and Han Fan to attack Liangfu.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Murong Zhen on Qing, Murong Yu on Xu, Murong Ning and Han Fan on Liangfu.

sentences.zh: 昱等攻莒城，拔之，徐州刺史段宏奔于魏。

translations.literal: Yu and the others attacked Jucheng, took it, and Inspector of Xu Duan Hong fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yu took Jucheng; Duan Hong ran to Wei.

sentences.zh: 封融又集群盜襲石塞城，殺鎮西大將軍余郁，青土振恐，人懷異議。

translations.literal: Feng Rong again gathered bandits to raid Stone Stockade Fort, killed General Who Guards the West Yu Yu, Qing soil shook in fear, and people harbored dissenting views.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Rong’s raiders killed Yu Yu; Qingzhou panicked and loyalty frayed.

sentences.zh: 慕容凝謀殺韓範，將襲廣固。

translations.literal: Murong Ning plotted to kill Han Fan and intended to strike Guanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ning meant to murder Han Fan and seize Guanggu.

sentences.zh: 範知而攻之，凝奔梁父。

translations.literal: Fan learned of it and attacked him; Ning fled to Liangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan struck first; Murong Ning fled to Liangfu.

sentences.zh: 范並其眾，攻梁父克之，凝奔姚興，慕容法出奔于魏。

translations.literal: Fan merged his host, attacked Liangfu and took it; Ning fled to Yao Xing; Murong Fa fled out to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan took Liangfu; Murong Ning fled to Yao Xing; Murong Fa to Wei.

sentences.zh: 慕容鎮克青州，鐘殺其妻子，為地道而出，單馬奔姚興。

translations.literal: Murong Zhen took Qingzhou; Zhong killed his wife and children, dug a tunnel to get out, and on a single horse fled to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Zhen conquered Qingzhou; Murong Zhong slaughtered his family, tunneled out, and galloped alone to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 于時超不恤政事，畋遊是好，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: At that time Chao did not care for government affairs; hunting and roaming were his delight; the common people suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao neglected rule for the hunt; the people groaned.

sentences.zh: 其僕射韓𧨳切諫，不納。

translations.literal: His vice director Han Zhuo remonstrated sternly; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Han Zhuo pleaded in vain.

sentences.zh: 超議復肉刑、九等之選，乃下書於境內曰：

translations.literal: Chao debated restoring corporal punishment and the nine-rank selection, and thereupon issued a proclamation within the borders, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He floated restoring mutilation penalties and nine-grade recruitment, and published a long edict:

sentences.zh: 陽九數纏，永康多難。

translations.literal: The yang-nine reckonings twine; Yongkang knew many hardships.
translations.idiomatic: “Ill-starred cycles and Yongkang’s woes—”

sentences.zh: 自北都傾陷，典章淪滅，律令法憲，靡有存者。

translations.literal: Since the northern capital overturned, canons sank away; statutes, ordinances, laws, and models—none survive.
translations.idiomatic: “—toppled the northern capital and swallowed the law.”

sentences.zh: 綱理天下，此焉為本，既不能導之以德，必須齊之以刑。

translations.literal: To order the All-under-Heaven, this is the root; since we cannot guide them with virtue, we must even them with punishments.
translations.idiomatic: “Rule needs law; without moral sway, use the rod.”

sentences.zh: 且虞舜大聖，猶命咎繇作士，刑之不可已已也如是！

translations.literal: Moreover Shun the great sage still ordered Gao Yao to be minister of crime—thus punishments cannot be stopped, stopped like this!
translations.idiomatic: “Even Shun set Gao Yao over justice—punishment is inescapable.”

sentences.zh: 先帝季興，大業草創，兵革尚繁，未遑修制。

translations.literal: The former emperor in his last rise, great enterprise still in the grass-creation stage, arms and armor still numerous, had no leisure to repair institutions.
translations.idiomatic: “Our founder was too busy fighting to codify law.”

sentences.zh: 朕猥以不德，嗣承大統，撫禦寡方，至蕭牆釁發，遂戎馬生郊，典儀寢廢。

translations.literal: We, mean in virtue, have inherited the great line, ruled and restrained without method, until trouble sprang within the bed curtain; then war-horses foaled in the suburbs and ceremony slept abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: “We inherited chaos, misruled until kin turned blades and armies trampled the suburbs.”

sentences.zh: 今四境無虞，所宜修定，尚書可召集公卿。

translations.literal: Now the four marches are without alarm; it is fitting to repair and fix; the Secretariat may summon the dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: “Now the frontiers are quiet—time to legislate; summon the ministers.”

sentences.zh: 至如不忠不孝若封嵩之輩，梟斬不足以痛之，宜致烹轘之法，亦可附之律條，納以大辟之科。

translations.literal: As for the disloyal and unfilial like Feng Song’s sort, beheading and display are not enough to pain them; boiling and tearing by cart should be applied; these too may be attached to the statutes, folded into the capital-crime articles.
translations.idiomatic: “Traitors like Feng Song deserve boiling and tearing, not mere beheading—write it into the code.”

sentences.zh: 肉刑者，乃先聖之經，不刊之典，漢文易之，輕重乖度。

translations.literal: Corporal punishment is the classic of former sages, an unalterable model; Emperor Wen of Han changed it, and light and heavy lost measure.
translations.idiomatic: “Mutilation was sage law; Han Wendi’s mercy upset proportion.”

sentences.zh: 今犯罪彌多，死者稍眾。

translations.literal: Now crimes grow ever more numerous; the dead become somewhat more many.
translations.idiomatic: “Crime swells; executions mount.”

sentences.zh: 肉刑之於化也，濟育既廣，懲慘尤深，光壽、建興中二祖已議復之，未及而晏駕。

translations.literal: As for corporal punishment in transformation, its nurturing aid is already broad, its deterrent cruelty especially deep; in Guangshou and Jianxing the two ancestors already debated restoring it, but before it could happen they died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: “Mutilation both deters and redeems; two late kings meant to revive it but died too soon.”

sentences.zh: 其令博士已上參考舊事，依《呂刑》及漢、魏、晉律令，消息增損，議成燕律。

translations.literal: Order erudites and above to consult former affairs, follow the ‘Lü Xing’ and Han, Wei, and Jin statutes and ordinances, adjust by increase and decrease, deliberate and complete Yan law.
translations.idiomatic: “Let scholars draft new Yan law from the Lü Xing and Han–Wei–Jin codes.”

sentences.zh: 五刑之屬三千，而罪莫大於不孝。

translations.literal: Among the three thousand articles of the five punishments, no crime is greater than unfilial piety.
translations.idiomatic: “Of three thousand clauses, none tops unfilial crime.”

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「非聖人者無法，非孝者無親，此大亂之道也。

translations.literal: Confucius said: “Those who deny sages have no law; those who deny filial piety have no kin—this is the way of great disorder.”
translations.idiomatic: Confucius: impiety and anti-sage doctrine unmake the state.

sentences.zh: 」轘裂之刑，烹煮之戮，雖不在五品之例，然亦行之自古。

translations.literal: ” Punishment of tearing by cart and boiling execution, though not in the five grades, have also been practiced since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Cart-tearing and cauldron killings, though outside the “five punishments,” are ancient tools.

sentences.zh: 渠彌之轘，著之《春秋》；

translations.literal: Qumi’s tearing is written in the ‘Spring and Autumn’;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhuang’s minister Qumi was torn apart—recorded in the Annals.

sentences.zh: 哀公之烹，爰自中代。

translations.literal: Duke Ai’s boiling comes from middle antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Ai’s boiling belongs to middle antiquity.

sentences.zh: 世宗都齊，亦湣刑罰失中，咨嗟寢食。

translations.literal: Shizong when he capital at Qi also pitied that punishments missed the mean and sighed, forgetting food and sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Our Shizong at Qi likewise fretted when justice skewed.

sentences.zh: 王者之有刑糾，猶人之左右手焉。

translations.literal: For a king to have punishments to correct is like a man’s left and right hands.
translations.idiomatic: Law to a king is like two hands to a man.

sentences.zh: 故孔子曰：「刑罰不中，則人無所措手足。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius said: “When punishments miss the mean, the people have nowhere to put hand or foot.”
translations.idiomatic: Confucius warned that skewed law leaves people helpless.

sentences.zh: 」是以蕭何定法令而受封，叔孫通以制儀為奉常。

translations.literal: ” Therefore Xiao He fixed statutes and received enfeoffment; Shu Sun Tong by making ritual became minister of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He and Shu Sun Tong won honor for codifying law and rite.

sentences.zh: 立功立事，古之所重。

translations.literal: To establish merit and affairs is what antiquity prized.
translations.idiomatic: Great deeds mattered to the ancients.

sentences.zh: 其明議損益，以成一代准式。

translations.literal: Let them clarify increase and decrease to complete a generation’s standard model.
translations.idiomatic: Debate amendments until we have a model code.

sentences.zh: 周、漢有貢士之條，魏立九品之選，二者孰愈，亦可詳聞。

translations.literal: Zhou and Han had articles for presenting scholars; Wei established nine-rank selection—which of the two is better may also be reported in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Compare Zhou–Han recommendation to Wei’s nine ranks.”

sentences.zh: 群下議多不同，乃止。

translations.literal: The host of subordinates debated, mostly disagreeing, and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Officials split; the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 超母妻既先在長安，為姚興所拘，責超稱籓，求太樂諸伎，若不可，使送吳口千人。

translations.literal: Chao’s mother and wife, since they were earlier in Chang’an, were detained by Yao Xing; Xing demanded Chao declare vassalage and send the Grand Music performers; if not, send a thousand Wu captives.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing held Murong Chao’s women hostage, demanding vassalage, the imperial musicians, or else a thousand southerners.

sentences.zh: 超下書遣群臣詳議。

translations.literal: Chao issued an edict ordering the host of ministers to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao asked his court for options.

sentences.zh: 左僕射段暉議曰：「太上囚楚，高祖不回。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Duan Hui argued: “When the Grand Supreme was imprisoned in Chu, the High Ancestor did not bend.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Hui cited Liu Bang refusing to ransom his father from Xiang Yu.

sentences.zh: 今陛下嗣守社稷，不宜以私親之故而降統天之尊。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty inherits and guards the altars of soil and grain; you ought not, because of private kinship, lower the honor that unifies heaven.
translations.idiomatic: A king must not demean the throne for captive kin.

sentences.zh: 又太樂諸伎，皆是前世伶人，不可與彼，使移風易俗，宜掠吳口與之。

translations.literal: Moreover the Grand Music performers are all former entertainers of prior ages—you cannot give them to him; let him shift custom by moving—better to raid Wu captives and give him those.”
translations.idiomatic: Never surrender the court orchestra—seize Jin subjects instead.”

sentences.zh: 」尚書張華曰：「若侵掠吳邊，必成鄰怨。

translations.literal: ” Minister Zhang Hua said: “If we raid Jin’s border, we are sure to complete neighborly resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua warned that slaving raids would poison relations with Jin.

sentences.zh: 此既能往，彼亦能來，兵連禍結，非國之福也。

translations.literal: This side can go there, that side can also come; arms linked and disaster knotted is not the state’s blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Tit-for-tat war helps no one.

sentences.zh: 昔孫權重黎庶之命，屈己以臣魏；

translations.literal: Anciently Sun Quan weighted the lives of the black-haired masses and bent himself to serve Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan once bowed to Wei to spare his people.

sentences.zh: 惠施惜愛子之頭，舍志以尊齊。

translations.literal: Hui Shi pitied his beloved son’s head and set aside his intent to honor Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Hui Shi yielded pride for a son’s life.

sentences.zh: 況陛下慈德在秦，方寸崩亂，宜暫降大號，以申至孝之情。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty’s kindly virtue lies in Qin; your heart is shattered in chaos—you ought temporarily to lower the great title to extend utmost filial feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao’s heart was in Chang’an—briefly swallow pride for his mother.

sentences.zh: 權變之道，典謨所許。

translations.literal: The way of weighing change is what the canons permit.
translations.idiomatic: Classics allow tactical humility.

sentences.zh: 韓范智能回物，辯足傾人，昔與姚興俱為秦太子中舍人，可遣將命，降號修和。

translations.literal: Han Fan’s intelligence can turn things, his eloquence enough to sway men; anciently he and Yao Xing were both attendants in the Eastern Palace of Qin—you can send him on mission to lower the title and repair peace.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan, Yao Xing’s old colleague, could negotiate a face-saving deal.

sentences.zh: 所謂屈於一人之下，申于萬人之上也。

translations.literal: This is what is called bowing beneath one man to stretch above ten thousand.”
translations.idiomatic: “Kneel to one ruler to save myriad subjects.”

sentences.zh: 」超大悅曰：「張尚書得吾心矣。

translations.literal: ” Chao was greatly pleased and said: “Director Zhang has gotten Our heart.”
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao cried that Zhang Hua read his mind.

sentences.zh: 」使范聘於興。

translations.literal: ” He sent Fan on embassy to Xing.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Han Fan to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 及至長安，興謂範曰：「封愷前來，燕王與朕抗禮。

translations.literal: When he reached Chang’an, Xing said to Fan: “Feng Kai came before; the Yan king treated Us as an equal by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing greeted Han Fan: last envoy Feng Kai had treated Qin as peer.

sentences.zh: 及卿至也，款然而附。

translations.literal: When you arrived he attached himself warmly.
translations.idiomatic: Now Murong Chao groveled.

sentences.zh: 為依春秋以小事大之義？

translations.literal: Is it following the Spring and Autumn meaning of the small serving the great?
translations.idiomatic: Was this the small state serving the great?

sentences.zh: 為當專以孝敬為母屈也？

translations.literal: Or is it solely bending in filial respect for the mother?”
translations.idiomatic: Or mere filial blackmail?

sentences.zh: 」範曰：「周爵五等，公侯異品，小大之禮，因而生焉。

translations.literal: ” Fan said: “Zhou’s nobility had five ranks; dukes and marquises differed in grade; rites of great and small arose from this.”
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan began with Zhou feudal ranks to frame parity.

sentences.zh: 今陛下命世龍興，光宅西秦，本朝主上承祖宗遺烈，定鼎東齊，中分天曜，南面並帝。

translations.literal: “Now Your Majesty, a dragon risen to command the age, shines in western Qin; our court’s sovereign inherits the fierce legacy of ancestors, fixes the cauldron in eastern Qi; you split heaven’s radiance, face south, and both are emperors.”
translations.idiomatic: He styled both courts as equal emperors splitting the mandate.

sentences.zh: 通聘結好，義尚廉沖，便至矜誕，苟折行人，殊似吳、晉爭盟，滕、薛競長，恐傷大秦堂堂之盛，有損皇燕巍巍之美，彼我俱失，竊未安之。

translations.literal: “Envoys exchange visits and knot friendship; the right meaning favors modesty—yet you strut and boast, casually humiliate the traveler—much like Wu and Jin vying in covenant, Teng and Xue competing for seniority; I fear it wounds great Qin’s majestic splendor and damages royal Yan’s towering grace; both sides lose—I privately am not at ease.”
translations.idiomatic: He warned Yao Xing that bullying an envoy shamed both realms.

sentences.zh: 」興怒曰：「若如卿言，便是非為大小而來。

translations.literal: ” Xing angrily said: “If it were as you say, then they did not come for reasons of great and small.”
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing snapped that Yan was not about rank.

sentences.zh: 」範曰：「雖由大小之義，亦緣寡君純孝過於重華，願陛下體敬親之道，霈然垂湣。

translations.literal: ” Fan said: “Though the meaning of great and small is involved, it is also because our poor ruler’s pure filial piety surpasses Shun’s; I hope Your Majesty will embody reverence for kin and pour forth pity.”
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan answered that Murong Chao’s filial piety exceeded Shun’s and begged mercy.

sentences.zh: 」興曰：「吾久不見賈生，自謂過之，今不及矣。

translations.literal: ” Xing said: “Long have I not seen Jia Yi; I thought myself his better—now I do not reach him.”
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing grudgingly compared him to Jia Yi.

sentences.zh: 」於是為范設舊交之禮，申敘平生，謂範曰：「燕王在此，朕亦見之，風表乃可，於機辯未也。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he treated Fan with the rites of an old acquaintance, narrating their whole lives, and said to Fan: “The Yan king here—We have also seen him; his bearing is passable, but in sharp debate he is not yet there.”
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing feasted Han Fan as an old friend, dismissing Murong Chao’s wit.

sentences.zh: 」範曰：「大辯若訥，聖人美之，況爾日龍潛鳳戢，和光同塵，若使負日月而行，則無繼天之業矣。

translations.literal: ” Fan said: “Great eloquence seems dull—the sage prized it; moreover that day the dragon hid and the phoenix folded, blending gleam with dust; had he shouldered sun and moon in his walk, there would be no enterprise to continue heaven.”
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan quoted “great eloquence seems slow” and said Murong Chao had hidden his light.

sentences.zh: 」興笑曰：「可謂使乎延譽者也。

translations.literal: ” Xing laughed and said: “You may be called one who on embassy spreads praise.”
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing laughed that he was the envoy who sings his master’s praise.

sentences.zh: 」範承間逞說，姚興大悅，賜范千金，許以超母妻還之。

translations.literal: ” Fan seized the interval to press his persuasion; Yao Xing was greatly pleased, gifted Fan a thousand in gold, and promised to return Chao’s mother and wife.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan pressed his case; Yao Xing relented, paid him, and promised the hostages back.

sentences.zh: 慕容凝自梁父奔于姚興，言於興曰：「燕王稱籓，本非推德，權為母屈耳。

translations.literal: Murong Ning fled from Liangfu to Yao Xing and said to Xing: “The Yan king’s declaration of vassalage was not from yielding virtue—it was a temporary bend for his mother.”
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ning warned that Murong Chao’s submission was a ruse for his mother.

sentences.zh: 古之帝王尚興師征質，豈可虛還其母乎！

translations.literal: “Ancient emperors still raised armies to demand hostages—how can you hollowly return his mother!”
translations.idiomatic: “Kings always demanded hostages—do not free her for nothing.”

sentences.zh: 母若一還，必不復臣也。

translations.literal: “If the mother returns once, he will surely not again be a subject.”
translations.idiomatic: “Once she is home he will rebel.”

sentences.zh: 宜先制其送伎，然後歸之。

translations.literal: “You ought first to seize the performers he is to send, then return her.”
translations.idiomatic: “Take the musicians first, then release her.”

sentences.zh: 」興意乃變，遣使聘於超。

translations.literal: ” Xing’s intent then changed; he sent envoys on a friendly visit to Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing wavered and reopened talks.

sentences.zh: 超遣其僕射張華、給事中宗正元入長安，送太樂伎一百二十人于姚興。

translations.literal: Chao sent his vice director Zhang Hua and attendant for miscellaneous purposes Zong Zhengyuan to Chang’an, delivering a hundred twenty Grand Music performers to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao sent Zhang Hua and Zong Zhengyuan with a hundred twenty court musicians.

sentences.zh: 興大悅，延華入宴。

translations.literal: Xing was greatly pleased and drew Hua into a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing feasted Zhang Hua.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，樂作，興黃門侍郎尹雅謂華曰：「昔殷之將亡，樂師歸周；

translations.literal: When the wine was deep and music began, Xing’s gentleman attendant at the yellow gate Yin Ya said to Hua: “Anciently when Yin was about to perish, the music masters went to Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ya taunted that Shang’s musicians had fled to Zhou before the fall.

sentences.zh: 今皇秦道盛，燕樂來庭。

translations.literal: “now imperial Qin’s Way flourishes and Yan’s music comes to court.”
translations.idiomatic: “Now Qin thrives and Yan’s orchestra kneels here.”

sentences.zh: 廢興之兆，見於此矣。

translations.literal: “The omens of decline and rise appear in this.”
translations.idiomatic: “Rise and fall show in this.”

sentences.zh: 」華曰：「自古帝王，為道不同，權譎之理，會于功成。

translations.literal: ” Hua said: “From antiquity emperors have differed in their Way; the pattern of weighing stratagem meets in merit accomplished.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua parried that different ages use different stratagems.

sentences.zh: 故老子曰：'將欲取之，必先與之。

translations.literal: “Therefore Laozi says: ‘If you would take, you must first give.’”
translations.idiomatic: He quoted Laozi on giving to take.

sentences.zh: '今總章西入，必由餘東歸，禍福之驗，此其兆乎！

translations.literal: “‘Now the Zongzhang goes west—surely the surplus will return east; is this not the omen of fortune and disaster!’”
translations.idiomatic: “Music west today means heads east tomorrow—mark the omen.”

sentences.zh: 」興怒曰：「昔齊、楚競辯，二國連師。

translations.literal: ” Xing angrily said: “Anciently Qi and Chu debated rhetoric; the two states linked armies.”
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing blustered about Qi–Chu rhetorical wars.

sentences.zh: 卿小國之臣，何敢抗衡朝士！

translations.literal: “You, a minister of a small state—how dare you stand up to courtiers!”
translations.idiomatic: “How dare a petty envoy mouth off?”

sentences.zh: 」華遜辭曰：「奉使之始，實願交歡上國，上國既遺小國之臣，辱及寡君社稷，臣亦何心，而不仰酬！

translations.literal: ” Hua deferentially said: “When the mission began, I truly wished to befriend the superior state; the superior state has now disdained the small state’s minister and insulted even our poor ruler’s altars—how could your servant lack heart and not answer upward!”
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua apologized yet stood his ground.

sentences.zh: 」興善之，於是還超母妻。

translations.literal: ” Xing approved of this; thereupon he returned Chao’s mother and wife.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing relented and freed Murong Chao’s family.

sentences.zh: ，追尊其父為穆皇帝，立其母段氏為皇太后，妻呼延氏為皇后。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his father as Emperor Mu, established his mother Lady Duan as empress dowager, and his wife Lady Huyan as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao canonized his father as Emperor Mu, made Lady Duan dowager, Lady Huyan empress.

sentences.zh: 祀南郊，將登壇，有獸大如馬，狀類鼠而色赤，集於圓丘之側，俄而不知所在。

translations.literal: He sacrificed at the southern suburb; about to ascend the altar, a beast as large as a horse, shaped like a rat but red in color, alighted beside the round mound; presently it was nowhere to be seen.
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban rites a red horse-sized rat-beast appeared on the mound, then vanished.

sentences.zh: 須臾大風暴起，天地晝昏，其行宮習儀皆振裂。

translations.literal: Before long a great windstorm arose; heaven and earth were dark as dusk by day; his traveling palace and rehearsal gear were all torn apart.
translations.idiomatic: A black wind shredded the ritual tents.

sentences.zh: 超懼，密問其太史令成公綏，對曰：「陛下信用奸臣，誅戮賢良，賦斂繁多，事役殷苦所致也。

translations.literal: Chao feared and secretly questioned his astrologer-in-chief Cheng Gong Sui, who answered: “It is caused by Your Majesty trusting wicked ministers, executing worthy good men, levies and corvée being numerous, labor and service oppressively bitter.”
translations.idiomatic: Astrologer Cheng Gong Sui blamed tyranny and taxes.

sentences.zh: 」超懼而大赦，譴責公孫五樓等。

translations.literal: ” Chao feared and granted great amnesty, blaming Gongsun Wulou and others.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao amnestied the realm and scolded Gongsun Wulou.

sentences.zh: 俄而復之。

translations.literal: Before long he restored them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he restored their favor.

sentences.zh: 是歲廣固地震，天齊水湧，井水溢，女水竭，河、濟凍合，而澠水不冰。

translations.literal: That year Guanggu earthquake; Tianqi waters surged; well water overflowed; the Lady River ran dry; the Yellow and Ji froze solid, yet the Mian River did not ice.
translations.idiomatic: Earthquake, floods, dry springs, frozen rivers—but the Mian stayed open: ill omens piled up.

sentences.zh: 超正旦朝群臣于東陽殿，聞樂作，歎音佾不備，悔送伎于姚興，遂議入寇。

translations.literal: Chao on New Year’s dawn faced the host of ministers in the Dongyang Hall; hearing the music play, he sighed that pitch-pipes and dancers were incomplete, regretted sending the performers to Yao Xing, and thereupon debated raiding south.
translations.idiomatic: New Year music shamed him—he had traded musicians to Qin—and he talked of invading Jin.

sentences.zh: 其領軍韓𧨳諫曰：「先帝以舊京傾沒，輯翼三齊，苟時運未可，上智輟謀。

translations.literal: His general-in-chief Han Zhuo remonstrated: “The former emperor, because the old capital overturned, gathered wings in the three Qi—if the hour of fate was not yet, the highest wisdom halts plans.”
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhuo begged him to remember Murong De’s caution.

sentences.zh: 今陛下嗣守成規，宜閉關養士，以待賦釁，不可結怨南鄰，廣樹仇隙。

translations.literal: “Now Your Majesty inherits and guards completed norms; you ought to close the passes and nurture troops, awaiting the enemy’s fault; you cannot knot resentment with the southern neighbor and broadly plant enmity.”
translations.idiomatic: He urged sealing the border, not provoking Jin.

sentences.zh: 」超曰：「我計已定，不與卿言。

translations.literal: ” Chao said: “Our plan is set; We will not speak with you.”
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao cut him off.

sentences.zh: 」於是遣其將斛谷提、公孫歸等率騎寇宿豫，陷之，執陽平太守劉千載、濟陰太守徐阮，大掠而去。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he sent his generals Huguti, Gongsun Gui, and others leading horse to raid Suyu, took it, seized Administrator of Yangping Liu Qianzai and Administrator of Jiyin Xu Ruan, and plundered greatly as they left.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Huguti and Gongsun Gui to seize Suyu, capture two Jin prefects, and loot.

sentences.zh: 簡男女二千五百，付太樂教之。

translations.literal: He selected twenty-five hundred men and women and handed them to the Grand Music to train.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed twenty-five hundred captives into the palace choir.

sentences.zh: 時公孫五樓為侍中、尚書，領左衛將軍，專總朝政，兄歸為冠軍、常山公，叔父頹為武衛、興樂公。

translations.literal: At that time Gongsun Wulou was palace attendant and minister, concurrent left guard general, monopolizing court government; his elder brother Gui was champion general and Duke of Changshan; his uncle Tui was martial guard and Duke of Xingle.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Wulou ran the court; his brother and uncle held great titles.

sentences.zh: 五樓宗親皆夾輔左右，王公內外無不憚之。

translations.literal: Wulou’s kin all flanked and assisted left and right; among princes and dukes inside and outside none did not fear them.
translations.idiomatic: The clan packed the palace; nobles trembled.

sentences.zh: 超論宿豫之功，封斛穀提等並為郡、縣公。

translations.literal: Chao debated the merit of the Suyu campaign and enfeoffed Huguti and the others as dukes of commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded the raiders with county duchies.

sentences.zh: 慕容鎮諫曰：「臣聞縣賞待勳，非功不侯，今公孫歸結禍延兵，殘賊百姓，陛下封之，得無不可乎！

translations.literal: Murong Zhen remonstrated: “Your servant has heard that county rewards await merit—without merit one is not enfeoffed; now Gongsun Gui tied on disaster and prolonged arms, maimed the hundred surnames—Your Majesty enfeoffs them—is it not impermissible!”
translations.idiomatic: Murong Zhen protested ennobling looters.

sentences.zh: 夫忠言逆耳，非親不發。

translations.literal: “Loyal words grate on the ear—if not kin they are not spoken.”
translations.idiomatic: “Only kin speak bitter truth.”

sentences.zh: 臣雖庸朽，忝國戚籓，輒盡愚款，惟陛下圖之。

translations.literal: “Though your servant is mean and rotten, I disgrace the state’s kin screen—I exhaust foolish sincerity; only Your Majesty consider it.”
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded as a kinsman.

sentences.zh: 」超怒，不答，自是百僚杜口，莫敢開言。

translations.literal: ” Chao grew angry and did not answer; from this the hundred officials sealed their mouths and none dared open speech.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao’s glare silenced the court.

sentences.zh: 尚書都令史王儼諂事五樓，遷尚書郎，出為濟南太守，入為尚書左丞，時人為之語曰：「欲得侯，事五樓。」

translations.literal: Secretariat chief clerk Wang Yan fawned on Wulou, was promoted ministerial secretary, went out as governor of Jinan, came in as left aide to the minister—people of the time made a saying: “If you want a marquis, serve Wulou.”
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Wang Yan curried Gongsun Wulou; the rhyme ran, “Want a fief? Flatter Wulou.”

sentences.zh: 又遣公孫歸等率騎三千入寇濟南，執太守趙元，略男女千餘人而去。

translations.literal: He again sent Gongsun Gui and others leading three thousand horse to raid Jinan, seized Governor Zhao Yuan, and carried off more than a thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Another raid took Jinan’s governor and slaves.

sentences.zh: 劉裕率師將討之，超引見群臣于節陽殿，議距王師。

translations.literal: Liu Yu led an army about to punish him; Chao led out the host of ministers in the Jieyang Hall to debate resisting the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: As Liu Yu marched, Murong Chao convened council at Jieyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 公孫五樓曰：「吳兵輕果，所利在戰，初鋒勇銳，不可爭也。

translations.literal: Gongsun Wulou said: “Wu’s troops are light and decisive; what they profit from is battle; the first clash is brave and sharp—it cannot be contested.”
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Wulou said Jin troops lived for the first shock.

sentences.zh: 宜據大峴，使不得入，曠日延時，沮其銳氣。

translations.literal: “You ought to hold Daxian Pass and keep them from entering; stretch days and lengthen time, sap their keen edge.”
translations.idiomatic: Hold Daxian and bleed their momentum.

sentences.zh: 可徐簡精騎二千，循海而南。

translations.literal: “You may leisurely select two thousand picked horse and follow the sea south.”
translations.idiomatic: Send two thousand picked cavalry along the coast.

sentences.zh: 絕其糧運，別敕段暉率兗州之軍，緣山東下。

translations.literal: “Cut their grain transport; separately order Duan Hui to lead Yan Province’s army down along the mountains east.”
translations.idiomatic: Strike their supply lines; have Duan Hui sweep down the eastern hills.

sentences.zh: 腹背擊之，上策也。

translations.literal: “Strike them belly and back—the upper strategy.”
translations.idiomatic: “Pinch them—that is the best plan.”

sentences.zh: 各命守宰，依險自固，校其資儲之外，餘悉焚蕩，芟除粟苗，使敵無所資。

translations.literal: “Order each defender to hold fast by natural barriers, and besides what their stores allow, burn all else, cut the grain shoots, so the enemy has nothing to draw on.”
translations.idiomatic: Scorch the earth behind strongpoints—that is the middle plan.

sentences.zh: 堅壁清野，以待其釁，中策也。

translations.literal: “Strong walls and cleared fields, awaiting their fault—the middle strategy.”
translations.idiomatic: Fortify and strip the countryside.

sentences.zh: 縱賊入峴，出城逆戰，下策也。

translations.literal: “Let the bandits enter the pass and meet them outside the city in battle—the lower strategy.”
translations.idiomatic: Let them through the pass and fight in the plain—the worst plan.

sentences.zh: 」超曰：「京都殷盛，戶口眾多，非可一時入守。

translations.literal: ” Chao said: “The capital is populous and rich; households and mouths are many—not possible to enter and defend in one moment.”
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao said Guanggu could not be cleared overnight.

sentences.zh: 青苗布野，非可卒芟。

translations.literal: “Green shoots blanket the wilds—not possible to cut down at once.”
translations.idiomatic: He refused to torch the spring wheat.

sentences.zh: 設使芟苗城守，以全性命，朕所不能。

translations.literal: “Suppose we cut the shoots and defend the city to preserve life—that is something We cannot do.”
translations.idiomatic: He would not scorch earth to survive.

sentences.zh: 今據五州之強，帶山河之固，戰車萬乘，鐵馬萬群，縱令過峴，至於平地，徐以精騎踐之，此成擒也。

translations.literal: “Now relying on the strength of five provinces, girded by mountains and rivers’ solidity, war chariots in myriads, armored horse in myriads—even if they cross the pass and reach level ground, We will slowly use picked horse to trample them—this is assured capture.”
translations.idiomatic: He boasted five provinces and myriad horse would crush Liu Yu on the plain.

sentences.zh: 」賀賴盧苦諫，不從，退謂五樓曰：「上不用吾計，亡無日矣。

translations.literal: ” Helailu remonstrated bitterly; he did not follow; he withdrew and said to Wulou: “The sovereign will not use my plan—destruction is not far off.”
translations.idiomatic: Helailu warned Gongsun Wulou the kingdom was doomed.

sentences.zh: 」慕容鎮曰：「若如聖旨，必須平原用馬為便，宜出峴逆戰，戰而不勝，猶可退守。

translations.literal: ” Murong Zhen said: “If it follows Your Sagely intent, on level ground using horse is convenient; you ought to go out of the pass and meet them in battle—if battle does not succeed, you may still withdraw and defend.”
translations.idiomatic: Murong Zhen said if plains favored cavalry, meet Liu Yu outside the pass.

sentences.zh: 不宜縱敵入峴，自貽窘逼。

translations.literal: “It is not right to let the enemy into the pass and bring embarrassment and pressure on yourself.”
translations.idiomatic: Letting Jin through the pass was suicidal.

sentences.zh: 昔成安君不守井陘之關，終屈于韓信；

translations.literal: “Anciently Chengan Jun did not guard the barrier of Jingxing and in the end submitted to Han Xin;
translations.idiomatic: Chengan Jun lost Jingxing to Han Xin.

sentences.zh: 諸葛瞻不據束馬之險，卒擒于鄧艾。

translations.literal: “Zhuge Zhan did not hold the peril of Shuma and in the end was captured by Deng Ai.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Zhan gave up Shuma and fell to Deng Ai.

sentences.zh: 臣以為天時不如地利，阻守大峴，策之上也。

translations.literal: “Your servant thinks heaven’s timing is not as good as earth’s advantage; blocking and holding Daxian is the top of strategies.”
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s hour mattered less than holding Daxian.

sentences.zh: 」超不從。

translations.literal: ” Chao did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao refused.

sentences.zh: 鎮出，謂韓𧨳曰：「主上既不能芟苗守險，又不肯徙人逃寇，酷似劉璋矣。

translations.literal: When Zhen came out, he said to Han Zhuo: “The sovereign can neither cut the shoots and hold the peril, nor will he move the people to flee the bandits—he closely resembles Liu Zhang.”
translations.idiomatic: Murong Zhen told Han Zhuo their king was another Liu Zhang.

sentences.zh: 今年國滅，吾必死之，卿等中華之士，復為文身矣。

translations.literal: “This year when the state is destroyed, I am sure to die for it; you gentlemen, scholars of the Hua heartland, will again become tattooed bodies.”
translations.idiomatic: He expected death and warned northerners they would be barbarized.

sentences.zh: 」超聞而大怒，收鎮下獄。

translations.literal: ” When Chao heard it he was greatly angry and seized Zhen and cast him into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao jailed Murong Zhen.

sentences.zh: 乃攝莒、梁父二戍，修城隍，簡士馬，畜銳以待之。

translations.literal: He then drew in the two garrisons of Ju and Liangfu, repaired walls and moats, selected troops and horse, and stored keen edge to await them.
translations.idiomatic: He pulled in Ju and Liangfu garrisons and dug in.

sentences.zh: 其夏，王師次東莞，超遣其左軍段暉、輔國賀賴盧等六將步騎五萬，進據臨朐。

translations.literal: That summer the royal army halted at Dongguan; Chao sent his left army Duan Hui, assistant state Helailu, and six other generals with fifty thousand foot and horse to advance and hold Linqu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu reached Dongguan; Murong Chao sent fifty thousand under Duan Hui and Helailu to Linqu.

sentences.zh: 俄而王師度峴，超懼，率卒四萬就暉等於臨朐，謂公孫五樓曰：「宜進據川源，晉軍至而失水，亦不能戰矣。

translations.literal: Presently the royal army crossed the pass; Chao feared, led forty thousand troops to join Hui and the others at Linqu, and said to Gongsun Wulou: “You ought to advance and hold the river sources—when the Jin army arrives and loses water, they cannot fight either.”
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yu crossed Daxian, Murong Chao rushed to Linqu and told Gongsun Wulou to seize the watercourses.

sentences.zh: 」五樓馳騎據之。

translations.literal: ” Wulou galloped horse to seize them.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Wulou raced to the fords.

sentences.zh: 劉裕前驅將軍孟龍符已至川源，五樓戰敗而返。

translations.literal: Liu Yu’s vanguard general Meng Longfu had already reached the river sources; Wulou was defeated in battle and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Longfu held the water; Gongsun Wulou fled.

sentences.zh: 裕遣諮議參軍檀韶率銳卒攻破臨朐，超大懼，單騎奔段暉于城南。

translations.literal: Yu sent staff adviser Tan Shao leading picked troops to break Linqu; Chao was greatly afraid, fled alone on horse to Duan Hui south of the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Shao stormed Linqu; Murong Chao bolted to Duan Hui.

sentences.zh: 暉眾又戰敗，裕軍人斬暉。

translations.literal: Hui’s host was again defeated in battle; Yu’s soldiers beheaded Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Hui’s line broke; Liu Yu’s men killed him.

sentences.zh: 超又奔還廣固，徙郭內人入保小城，使其尚書郎張綱乞師于姚興。

translations.literal: Chao again fled back to Guanggu, moved the people inside the outer wall into the lesser city for protection, and sent his ministerial secretary Zhang Gang to beg troops from Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao shrank into Guanggu’s inner town and sent Zhang Gang to Qin for aid.

sentences.zh: 赦慕容鎮，進錄尚書、都督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: He pardoned Murong Zhen, promoted him recorder of the Secretariat and area commander of all military affairs at court and in the field.
translations.idiomatic: He freed Murong Zhen and made him chief minister and supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 引見群臣，謝之曰：「朕嗣奉成業，不能委賢任善，而專固自由，覆水不收，悔將何及！

translations.literal: He led out the host of ministers, apologized to them, saying: “We have inherited and upheld the completed enterprise, unable to delegate worthies and employ the good, but stubbornly free in Our own way—spilled water is not gathered; what regret can reach it!”
translations.idiomatic: He confessed he had misruled and spilled irretrievable water.

sentences.zh: 智士逞謀，必在事危，忠臣立節，亦在臨難，諸君其勉思六奇，共濟艱運。

translations.literal: “Wise men deploy stratagem surely when affairs are perilous; loyal ministers establish integrity also on facing disaster—may you all strive to think the six marvels and together ford hard fate.”
translations.idiomatic: He begged for Chen Ping–style stratagems in crisis.

sentences.zh: 」鎮進曰：「百姓之心，系於一人。

translations.literal: ” Zhen stepped forward and said: “The hearts of the hundred surnames hang on one man.”
translations.idiomatic: Murong Zhen said the people hung on the throne.

sentences.zh: 陛下既躬率六軍，身先奔敗，群臣解心，士庶喪氣，內外之情，不可復恃。

translations.literal: “Your Majesty has already personally led the six armies and taken the lead in rout; the host of ministers’ hearts are undone, gentry and common lose breath; inside and outside feelings cannot again be relied on.”
translations.idiomatic: His personal rout had broken morale.

sentences.zh: 如聞西秦自有內難，恐不暇分兵救人，正當更決一戰，以爭天命。

translations.literal: “As I hear, western Qin has its own internal troubles—I fear they have no leisure to divide troops to save others; you ought rightly to decide another battle to contest heaven’s mandate.”
translations.idiomatic: Qin was busy with civil war—no rescue—only one more field battle remained.

sentences.zh: 今散卒還者，猶有數萬，可悉出金帛、宮女，餌令一戰。

translations.literal: “Now scattered soldiers returning still number in the tens of thousands—you can bring out all gold, silks, and palace women as bait to force one battle.”
translations.idiomatic: He proposed spending treasury and concubines to buy one last stand.

sentences.zh: 天若相我，足以破賊。

translations.literal: “If heaven assists us, it is enough to break the bandits.”
translations.idiomatic: “If heaven favors us, we break Liu Yu.”

sentences.zh: 如其不濟，死尚為美，不可閉門坐受圍擊。

translations.literal: “If it does not succeed, death is still beautiful; you cannot close the gates and sit receiving siege blows.”
translations.idiomatic: “Better die charging than starve behind walls.”

sentences.zh: 」司徒慕容惠曰：「不然。

translations.literal: ” Minister of education Murong Hui said: “It is not so.”
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui disagreed.

sentences.zh: 今晉軍乘勝，有陵人之氣，敗軍之將，何以禦之！

translations.literal: “Now the Jin army rides victory and has the air of lording over others—how can a defeated host’s general oppose it!”
translations.idiomatic: Broken troops could not face Liu Yu’s wave.

sentences.zh: 秦雖與勃勃相持，不足為患。

translations.literal: “Though Qin is locked with Bobo, it is not enough to count as worry.”
translations.idiomatic: Helian Bobo kept Qin busy but not helpless.

sentences.zh: 且二國連橫，勢成脣齒，今有寇難，秦必救我。

translations.literal: “Moreover the two states are joined in horizontal alliance; the situation forms lips and teeth—now there is raider disaster, Qin is sure to save us.”
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Qin were allies—Qin would send help.

sentences.zh: 但自古乞援，不遣大臣則不致重兵，是以趙隸三請，楚師不出；

translations.literal: “But from antiquity when begging aid, if you do not send a great minister you do not draw heavy troops—therefore Zhao’s thrice begging indentured no Chu army;
translations.idiomatic: Envoys must be grandees—small fry fetch nothing.

sentences.zh: 平原一使，援至從成。

translations.literal: “one mission from Pingyuan and aid arrived and success followed.”
translations.idiomatic: Pingyuan Jun’s one embassy brought troops.

sentences.zh: 尚書令韓范德望具瞻，燕秦所重，宜遣乞援，以濟時難。

translations.literal: “Minister Secretary Han Fan’s virtue and gaze are looked up to by both Yan and Qin—you ought to send him to beg aid to ford the hour’s hardship.”
translations.idiomatic: Send Han Fan—respected in both courts—to Qin.

sentences.zh: 」於是遣范與王蒲乞師于姚興。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he sent Fan and Wang Pu to beg troops from Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Han Fan and Wang Pu to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，裕師圍城，四面皆合。

translations.literal: Before long, Yu’s army surrounded the city; on four sides all joined.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liu Yu ringed Guanggu.

sentences.zh: 人有竊告裕軍曰：「若得張綱為攻具者，城乃可得耳。

translations.literal: Someone secretly told the Yu army: “If you could get Zhang Gang to make siege engines, the city could be taken.”
translations.idiomatic: A traitor said Zhang Gang built siege gear.

sentences.zh: 」是月，綱自長安歸，遂奔於裕。

translations.literal: ” That month, Gang returned from Chang’an and thereupon fled to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: That month Zhang Gang returned from Chang’an and defected to Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 裕令綱周城大呼曰：「勃勃大破秦軍，無兵相救。

translations.literal: Yu ordered Gang to circle the wall and shout loudly: “Bobo has crushed Qin’s army—there are no troops to save you.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu had Zhang Gang shout that Helian Bobo had shattered Qin—no relief would come.

sentences.zh: 」超怒，伏弩射之，乃退。

translations.literal: ” Chao grew angry, laid ambush crossbows and shot at him; he then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao’s archers drove Zhang Gang back.

sentences.zh: 右僕射張華、中丞封愷並為裕軍所獲。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Zhang Hua and palace secretary Feng Kai were both captured by Yu’s army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua and Feng Kai fell prisoner.

sentences.zh: 裕令華、愷與超書，勸令早降。

translations.literal: Yu ordered Hua and Kai to write Chao a letter urging early surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu made them write Murong Chao to yield.

sentences.zh: 超乃遺裕書，請為籓臣，以大峴為界，並獻馬千區，以通和好，裕弗許。

translations.literal: Chao then sent Yu a letter, asking to be a vassal minister, with Daxian Pass as the boundary, and offered a thousand teams of horses to open good relations; Yu did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao offered vassalage, Daxian as border, and a thousand horses; Liu Yu refused.

sentences.zh: 江南繼兵相尋而至。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi reinforcements arrived one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh Jin regiments kept landing from the south.

sentences.zh: 尚書張俊自長安還，又降於裕，說容曰：「今燕人所以固守者，外杖韓范，冀得秦援。

translations.literal: Minister Zhang Jun returned from Chang’an and again surrendered to Yu, saying to Yu: “Now the reason Yan men stubbornly defend is they outwardly lean on Han Fan, hoping to gain Qin’s rescue.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun defected and told Liu Yu Yan held out for promised Qin aid under Han Fan.

sentences.zh: 范既時望，又與姚興舊昵，若勃勃敗後，秦必救燕，宜密信誘範，啖以重利，范來則燕人絕望，自然降矣。

translations.literal: “Fan is both the man of the hour and old-intimate with Yao Xing; if after Bobo’s defeat Qin is sure to save Yan, you ought secretly to write enticing Fan with rich profit—when Fan comes the Yan men will despair and naturally surrender.”
translations.idiomatic: He urged bribing Han Fan away from Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 」裕從之，表範為散騎常侍，遺範書以招之。

translations.literal: ” Yu followed this, memorialized Fan as cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and sent Fan a letter to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu offered Han Fan a Jin title and a letter.

sentences.zh: 時姚興乃遣其將姚強率步騎一萬，隨範就其將姚紹於洛陽，並兵來援。

translations.literal: At that time Yao Xing then sent his general Yao Qiang leading ten thousand foot and horse to follow Fan and join his general Yao Shao at Luoyang, merging troops to come to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing dispatched Yao Qiang with ten thousand men to Luoyang to reinforce Han Fan.

sentences.zh: 會赫連勃勃大破秦軍，興追強還長安。

translations.literal: It happened that Helian Bobo crushed Qin’s army; Xing recalled Qiang to Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Bobo routed Qin; Yao Xing recalled the relief column.

sentences.zh: 範歎曰：「天其滅燕乎！

translations.literal: Fan sighed: “Is Heaven about to extinguish Yan!”
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan groaned that heaven was killing Yan.

sentences.zh: 」會得裕書，遂降於裕。

translations.literal: ” When he received Yu’s letter, he thereupon surrendered to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He read Liu Yu’s offer and defected.

sentences.zh: 裕謂範曰：「卿欲立申包胥之功，何以虛還也？

translations.literal: Yu said to Fan: “You wished to establish Shen Baoxu’s merit—why return empty?”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu mocked him for failing like a hollow Shen Baoxu.

sentences.zh: 」範曰：「自亡祖司空世荷燕寵，故泣血秦庭，冀匡禍難。

translations.literal: ” Fan said: “Since my late grandfather the minister of works, generations have borne Yan’s favor; therefore I wept blood in Qin’s court, hoping to right disaster.”
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan said his family owed Yan generations of grace.

sentences.zh: 屬西朝多故，丹誠無效，可謂天喪弊邑而贊明公。

translations.literal: “It fell out that the western court had many troubles, and my crimson loyalty had no effect—one may say Heaven destroyed our poor town to aid the enlightened duke.”
translations.idiomatic: Qin’s chaos voided his mission; fate favored Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 智者見機而作，敢不至乎！

translations.literal: “The wise see the moment and act—how dare I not arrive!”
translations.idiomatic: “Wise men seize the hour—I came.”

sentences.zh: 」翌日，裕將範循城，由是人情離駭，無復固志，裕謂範曰：「卿宜至城下，告以禍福。

translations.literal: ” The next day Yu led Fan around the wall; on that account human hearts split in terror, none again had firm will; Yu said to Fan: “You ought to go below the wall and announce fortune and disaster.”
translations.idiomatic: Next day Liu Yu paraded Han Fan around the walls, then told him to shout defiance at the garrison.

sentences.zh: 」範曰：「雖蒙殊寵，猶未忍謀燕。

translations.literal: ” Fan said: “Though I have received extraordinary favor, I still cannot bear to plot against Yan.”
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan refused to harangue his old kingdom.

sentences.zh: 」裕嘉而不強，左右勸超誅範家，以止後叛。

translations.literal: ” Yu praised him and did not force him; those at Chao’s side urged Chao to execute Fan’s family to stop later defections.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu respected his silence; courtiers begged Murong Chao to slaughter Han Fan’s kin.

sentences.zh: 超知敗在旦夕，又弟𧨳盡忠無貳，故不罪焉。

translations.literal: Chao knew defeat was at dawn or dusk, and moreover younger brother Han Zhuo was utterly loyal without twofold intent; therefore he did not punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao spared Han Fan’s people because his brother Han Zhuo stayed loyal.

sentences.zh: 是歲東萊雨血，廣固城門鬼夜哭。

translations.literal: That year Donglai rained blood; Guanggu’s city gates heard ghosts weep by night.
translations.idiomatic: Blood rain fell; ghosts wailed at the gates.

sentences.zh: 明年朔旦，超登天門，朝群臣於城上，殺馬以饗將士，文武皆有遷授。

translations.literal: The next year on new moon dawn Chao ascended the Heavenly Gate, faced the host of ministers atop the wall, slaughtered horses to feast generals and officers; civil and martial all received promotions.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year’s dawn he feasted the garrison on horseflesh and handed out ranks.

sentences.zh: 超幸姬魏夫人從超登城，見王師之盛，握超手而相對泣，韓𧨳諫曰：「陛下遭百六之會，正是勉強之秋，而反對女子悲泣，何其鄙也！

translations.literal: Chao’s favored concubine Lady Wei followed Chao onto the wall; seeing the royal army’s might, she grasped Chao’s hand and wept face to face; Han Zhuo remonstrated: “Your Majesty meets the hundred-six conjunction—this is exactly the season to strive hard—yet you face a woman weeping—how base!”
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wei wept at Liu Yu’s host; Han Zhuo scolded Murong Chao for sniveling with a woman.

sentences.zh: 」超拭目謝之。

translations.literal: ” Chao wiped his eyes and thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao wiped his tears and thanked him.

sentences.zh: 其尚書令董銳勸超出降，超大怒，系之於獄。

translations.literal: His minister secretary Dong Rui urged Chao to go out and surrender; Chao grew greatly angry and bound him in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Secretary Dong Rui advised surrender; Murong Chao jailed him.

sentences.zh: 於是賀賴盧、公孫五樓為地道出戰王師，不利。

translations.literal: Thereupon Helailu and Gongsun Wulou dug a tunnel to go out and fight the royal army; it went ill.
translations.idiomatic: Helailu and Gongsun Wulou sallied by tunnel and lost.

sentences.zh: 河間人玄文說裕曰：「昔趙攻曹嶷，望氣者以為澠水帶城，非可攻拔，若塞五龍口，城必自陷。

translations.literal: A man of Hejian, Xuan Wen, said to Yu: “Anciently when Zhao attacked Cao Yi, the qi-watcher thought the Mian River girdled the city and it could not be stormed; if you block the Wulong mouth, the city is sure to collapse of itself.”
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Wen recalled damming Wulongkou to dry Cao Yi’s city—same trick for Guanggu.

sentences.zh: 石季龍從之，而嶷請降。

translations.literal: Shi Hu followed this, and Yi asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu dammed the river; Cao Yi yielded.

sentences.zh: 後慕容恪之圍段龕，亦如之，而龕降。

translations.literal: Later when Murong Ke besieged Duan Kan, he did likewise, and Kan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke did the same to Duan Kan.

sentences.zh: 降後無幾，又震開之。

translations.literal: Not long after surrender, it again quaked open.
translations.idiomatic: After each fall the dyke burst again.

sentences.zh: 今舊基猶在，可塞之。

translations.literal: “Now the old foundation still exists—you can block it.”
translations.idiomatic: “The old dam site remains—seal it.”

sentences.zh: 」裕從其言。

translations.literal: ” Yu followed his words.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu dammed the water.

sentences.zh: 至是，城中男女患腳弱病者太半。

translations.literal: At this point more than half the men and women in the city suffered foot-weakness illness.
translations.idiomatic: Half the city sickened with leg-rot.

sentences.zh: 超輦而升城，尚書悅壽言於超曰：「天地不仁，助寇為虐，戰士尪病，日就凋隕，守困窮城，息望外援，天時人事，亦可知矣。

translations.literal: Chao was carried in a palanquin up the wall; Minister Yue Shou spoke to Chao: “Heaven and earth are not humane—they aid the bandit in cruelty; warriors are wasted and sick, daily nearing withering fall; we guard a poor exhausted city, breath stopped waiting for outside aid—heaven’s timing and human affairs are also knowable.”
translations.idiomatic: Yue Shou said heaven sided with Liu Yu; the garrison was crippled and alone.

sentences.zh: 苟曆運有終，堯、舜降位，轉禍為福，聖達以先。

translations.literal: “If the allotted reign has an end, Yao and Shun yielded the throne—turning disaster to fortune is what the sage and clear do first.”
translations.idiomatic: He urged abdication like sage-kings.

sentences.zh: 宜追許、鄭之蹤，以全宗廟之重。

translations.literal: “You ought to follow the tracks of Xu and Zheng to preserve the weight of the ancestral temple.”
translations.idiomatic: Imitate rulers who quit to save the shrines.

sentences.zh: 」超歎曰：「廢興，命也。

translations.literal: ” Chao sighed: “Decline and rise are fate.”
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao answered that rise and fall were fate.

sentences.zh: 吾寧奮劍決死，不能銜璧求生。

translations.literal: “I would rather brandish the sword and decide death than hold the jade disk and beg life.”
translations.idiomatic: “I will die fighting, not surrender with seal in hand.”

sentences.zh: 」於是張綱為裕造沖車，覆以版屋，蒙之以皮，並設諸奇巧，城上火石弓矢無所施用；

translations.literal: ” Thereupon Zhang Gang for Yu made battering rams, roofed with plank houses, covered in hide, and installed every clever device—on the wall fire, stones, and bows had nothing they could apply;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gang built armored rams impervious to missiles.

sentences.zh: 又為飛樓、懸梯、木幔之屬，遙臨城上。

translations.literal: he also made flying towers, hanging ladders, wooden screens, and the like, overlooking the wall from afar.
translations.idiomatic: He added siege towers and mantlets.

sentences.zh: 超大怒，懸其母而支解之。

translations.literal: Chao grew greatly angry, hung up Gang’s mother and dismembered her.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao butchered Zhang Gang’s mother in rage.

sentences.zh: 城中出降者相繼。

translations.literal: Those who came out of the city to surrender followed one another.
translations.idiomatic: Defectors streamed out.

sentences.zh: 裕四面進攻，殺傷其眾，悅壽遂開門以納王師。

translations.literal: Yu attacked on four sides, killing and wounding his host; Yue Shou then opened the gate to admit the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu stormed every face; Yue Shou opened the gates.

sentences.zh: 超與左右數十騎出亡，為裕軍所執。

translations.literal: Chao with several tens of horse of his attendants fled out and was seized by Yu’s army.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao fled with dozens of riders and was caught.

sentences.zh: 裕數之以不降之狀，超神色自若，一無所言，惟以母托劉敬宣而已。

translations.literal: Yu enumerated his crimes of not surrendering; Chao’s spirit and bearing were self-possessed, he said nothing at all, only entrusted his mother to Liu Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu rebuked him; Murong Chao stayed silent, begging only that his mother be given to Liu Jingxuan.

sentences.zh: 送建康市斬之，時年二十六。

translations.literal: He was sent to Jiankang market and beheaded, aged twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: They executed him at twenty-six in the Jiankang marketplace.

sentences.zh: 在位六年。

translations.literal: He had reigned six years.
translations.idiomatic: Six years on the throne.

sentences.zh: 德以安帝僭位，至超二世，凡十一年，以滅。

translations.literal: De had usurped the throne under Emperor An; down to Chao two generations, in all eleven years, and so was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: From Murong De’s usurpation to Murong Chao—two reigns, eleven years—Yan ended.

sentences.zh: 慕容鍾

translations.literal: Murong Zhong
translations.idiomatic: Murong Zhong

sentences.zh: 慕容鐘，字道明，德從弟也。

translations.literal: Murong Zhong, courtesy name Daoming, was De’s younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Zhong, style Daoming, was Murong De’s cousin.

sentences.zh: 少有識量，喜怒不形於色，機神秀髮，言論清辯。

translations.literal: In youth he had judgment and capacity; joy and anger did not show on his face; his wit was bright and hair splendid, his speech clear in debate.
translations.idiomatic: Even young he was imperturbable, brilliant, and eloquent.

sentences.zh: 至於臨難對敵，智勇兼濟，累進奇策，德用之頗中。

translations.literal: When it came to facing disaster and opposing the enemy, wisdom and courage both helped; he repeatedly advanced marvelous plans, and De employed them and they mostly hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: In crisis he paired courage with stratagem; Murong De’s best moves were often his.

sentences.zh: 由是政無大小，皆以委之，遂為佐命無勳。

translations.literal: On that account, whether government was great or small, all was delegated to him; he thereupon became a founding assistant without [parallel] merit.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De handed him every lever of power—chief architect of the new state.

sentences.zh: 後公孫五樓規挾威權，慮鐘抑己，因勸超誅之，鐘遂謀反。

translations.literal: Later Gongsun Wulou schemed to monopolize awesomeness and authority, feared Zhong would check him, and therefore urged Chao to execute him; Zhong thereupon plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Wulou feared him and talked Murong Chao into killing him; Murong Zhong rebelled.

sentences.zh: 事敗，奔于姚興，興拜始平太守、歸義侯。

translations.literal: The affair failed; he fled to Yao Xing; Xing appointed him governor of Shiping and Marquis Who Returns to Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He lost, fled to Yao Xing, and became governor of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 封孚

translations.literal: Feng Fu
translations.idiomatic: Feng Fu

sentences.zh: 封孚，字處道，渤海蓚人也。

translations.literal: Feng Fu, courtesy name Chudao, was a man of Tiao in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Fu, style Chudao, hailed from Tiao in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 祖悛，振威將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Jun, General Who Rouses Might.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Feng Jun was a general.

sentences.zh: 父放，慕容垂之世吏部尚書。

translations.literal: His father was Fang, minister of personnel in Murong Chui’s age.
translations.idiomatic: His father Feng Fang ran personnel under Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 孚幼而聰敏和裕，有士君子之稱。

translations.literal: Fu in youth was clever, quick, mild, and generous, and had the reputation of a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Clever, gentle, and generous, he passed for a junzi.

sentences.zh: 寶僭位，累遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Bao usurped the throne, he was promoted repeatedly to minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Under Murong Bao he rose to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 及蘭汗之篡，南奔辟閭渾，渾表為渤海太守。

translations.literal: When Lan Han usurped, he fled south to Pilü Hun; Hun memorialized him as governor of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: He fled Lan Han to Pilü Hun, who made him Bohai governor.

sentences.zh: 德至莒城，孚出降，德曰：「朕平青州，不以為慶，喜於得卿也。

translations.literal: When De reached Jucheng, Fu came out to surrender; De said: “We pacify Qingzhou without taking it as celebration—Our joy is in gaining you.”
translations.idiomatic: Murong De said Qingzhou meant less than winning Feng Fu.

sentences.zh: 」常外總機事，內參密謀，雖位任崇重，謙虛博納，甚有大臣之體。

translations.literal: ” He always managed outward machinery of state and inward joined secret plots; though rank and duty were lofty and heavy, he was humble and broadly receptive—very much in the manner of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: He ran state business and counsel with modest grace.

sentences.zh: 及超嗣位，政出權嬖，多違舊章，軌憲日頹，殘虐滋甚，孚屢盡匡救，超不能納也。

translations.literal: When Chao succeeded, government issued from powerful favorites, much violated old norms, tracks and statutes daily declined, cruelty and slaughter grew worse—Fu repeatedly exhausted himself in rescue; Chao could not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Murong Chao favorites rotted the law; Feng Fu’s protests went unheard.

sentences.zh: 後臨軒謂孚曰：「朕于百王可方誰？

translations.literal: Later facing the gallery he said to Fu: “Among the hundred kings, whom may We match?”
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao once asked which emperor he resembled.

sentences.zh: 」孚對曰：「桀紂之主。

translations.literal: ” Fu answered: “Lords Jie and Zhou.”
translations.idiomatic: Feng Fu said Jie and Zhou—the worst tyrants.

sentences.zh: 」超大慚怒。

translations.literal: ” Chao was greatly ashamed and angry.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao flushed with rage.

sentences.zh: 孚徐步而出，不為改容。

translations.literal: Fu walked out slowly and did not change expression.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Fu strolled out unruffled.

sentences.zh: 司空鞠仲失色，謂孚曰：「與天子言，何其亢厲，宜應還謝。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Ju Zhong lost color and said to Fu: “Speaking with the Son of Heaven—how so harsh? You ought to go back and apologize.”
translations.idiomatic: Ju Zhong begged him to apologize to the throne.

sentences.zh: 」孚曰：「行年七十，墓木已拱，惟求死所耳。

translations.literal: ” Fu said: “I walk my seventieth year; the tomb tree already arches—I only seek a place to die.”
translations.idiomatic: Feng Fu said he was seventy and ready for the grave.

sentences.zh: 」竟不謝。

translations.literal: ” In the end he did not apologize.
translations.idiomatic: He never apologized.

sentences.zh: 以超三年死于家，時年七十一。

translations.literal: He died at home in Chao’s third year, aged seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-one in Murong Chao’s third year.

sentences.zh: 文筆多傳於世。

translations.literal: Much of his literary brush circulates in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His writings survived him.

sentences.zh: 【評贊】

translations.literal: 【Appraisal and eulogy】
translations.idiomatic: Historian’s appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：慕容德以季父之親，居鄴中之重，朝危未聞其節，君存遽踐其位，豈人理哉！

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Murong De, by kinship of youngest uncle, occupied Ye’s heavy post; with the court in peril he was not heard to show integrity, yet while the lord lived he hastily mounted the throne—is this human order!
translations.idiomatic: The chronicler faults Murong De for seizing the throne while kin still ruled.

sentences.zh: 然稟倜儻之雄姿，韞縱橫之遠略，屬分崩之運，成角逐之資，跨有全齊，竊弄神器，撫劍而爭衡秦、魏，練甲而志靜荊、吳，崇儒術以弘風，延讜言而勵己，觀其為國，有足稱焉。

translations.literal: Yet he received a free hero’s mien and stored a strategist’s far-reaching plan; he met a time of shattering apart and completed a capital for rivalry; he strode over all Qi, stole the divine regalia, fondled the sword to contend evenly with Qin and Wei, drilled armor intending to quiet Jing and Wu, honored Confucian arts to widen custom, drew out frank words to spur himself—in observing how he ran a state, there is enough to praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as a ruler he held Qi, jousted with Qin and Wei, promoted learning and counsel—much to admire.

sentences.zh: 超繼已成之基，居霸者之業，政刑莫恤，畋遊是好，杜忠良而讒佞進，暗聽受而勳戚離，先緒俄頹，家聲莫振，陷宿豫而貽禍，啟大峴而延敵，君臣就虜，宗廟為墟。

translations.literal: Chao inherited a completed foundation and occupied a hegemon’s enterprise, yet cared nothing for government or punishments, delighted in hunting and roaming, blocked the loyal and good while slanderers advanced, listened in darkness so merit kin departed; prior threads soon fell, house voice did not rise; he fell on Suyu and bequeathed disaster, opened Daxian and drew the enemy—lord and ministers became captives, the ancestral temple became a ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao squandered Murong De’s legacy, provoked Jin, and destroyed the state.

sentences.zh: 跡其人謀，非不幸也。

translations.literal: Tracing his human planning, it is not mere misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: His fall was earned, not bad luck alone.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：德實奸雄，轉敗為功。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: De was truly a crafty hero who turned defeat to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Verse: Murong De turned defeat to triumph.

sentences.zh: 奄有青土，淫名域中。

translations.literal: He suddenly possessed Qing’s soil, an excessive name within the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the eastern plain and styled himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 超承偽祚，撓其國步。

translations.literal: Chao inherited the usurped throne and twisted the state’s step.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao wrecked what he inherited.

sentences.zh: 廟失良籌，庭悲沾露。

translations.literal: The temple lost good plans; the court weeps dew-stained grief.
translations.idiomatic: Bad counsel drowned the altars in tears.
